scientific_question: How does the homogeneous Ir(III)-catalyzed annulation of 3-(phenanthren-4-yl)-1H-indazole with diphenylacetylene form the specified diaza[6]helicene, and how does the specified axially chiral nitrile–phosphine oxide ligand influence helicity selection and the relative kinetic difficulty of the connected product-forming chemistry?

inputs.content: 3-(phenanthren-4-yl)-1H-indazole, C21H14N2; indazole C3 is attached to phenanthrene C4 and the starting tautomer has N1-H. The substrate graph is in data/inputs/identities.json.
Diphenylacetylene, C14H10; its connectivity is in data/inputs/identities.json.

2'-(Diphenylphosphoryl)-[1,1'-binaphthalene]-2-carbonitrile, C33H22NOP. Use the specific axial enantiomer defined by the graph and oriented-volume sign in data/inputs/identities.json, not an unspecified racemate.

Substrate 0.10 mmol, diphenylacetylene 0.20 mmol (2.0 equivalents), [CpIrCl2]2 precursor dimer (5 mol% of dimer), the specified chiral ligand (20 mol%), AgOTf (2.5 equivalents), and H2O (10 equivalents) in dichloromethane (1.0 mL), under Ar at 50 °C for 36 h. All loadings are relative to substrate. Cp is the 1-tert-butyl-2,3,4,5-tetramethylcyclopentadienyl ligand specified in data/inputs/identities.json; do not substitute pentamethylcyclopentadienyl.

The annulation affords the product specified in PI6 in 82% isolated yield and 91% enantiomeric excess under the conditions in PI4. These are isolated-product endpoint observations, not an elementary rate measurement.

The observed product is (M)-5,6-diphenylindazolo[3,2-a]naphtho[2,1-h]isoquinoline, C35H22N2. Its M helical configuration is assigned by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. The product connectivity is in data/inputs/identities.json.
